reason: Rewrite [n choose r]_q as P_n(q)/(P_r(q)P_{n-r}(q)), where P_m(q)=product_{j=1}^m(1-q^j). This gives the symmetry [n choose r]_q=[n choose n-r]_q, so the hypothesis reduces to the quotient [n choose k0]_q/[n choose l0]_q being polynomial. If k0<l0, then with a=k0 and b=l0 one gets F(q)=A(q)/B(q), where A uses exponents a+1,...,b and B uses exponents n-b+1,...,n-a. Because a<b<=n/2, we have n-a>b. At a primitive (n-a)-th root of unity, all factors of A are nonzero, while the factor 1-q^(n-a) in B vanishes. Hence A/B cannot equal a polynomial. Contradiction. Therefore k0>=l0.
